title: Consolidate single-block Boolean admission across CPU and CUDA physical packers

masterplan.active_gate: Gate 1 — Renovation, owner-directed Genesis and general computer assistance

question: Can the residual CPU/CUDA single-block semantic admission duplication identified by GPU-177 be removed without adding another abstraction or moving physical backend constraints into Fourfold semantics?

implementation.pair_composition: validate_boolean_operands composes validate_boolean_block for both operands and retains only pair-level exact Fourfold subject and exact typed middle-axis requirements.
implementation.cpu: cpu_bitset_baseline.pack_rows delegates semantic block admission to validate_boolean_block and retains only Python-int bit packing locally.
implementation.cuda: cuda_boolean_probe._dense_from_block delegates semantic block admission to validate_boolean_block and retains dense CUDA allocation/scatter locally.
implementation.focused_regression: tests pin both physical modules to the exact shared validator object, pin pair admission to that same owner, and prove direct CPU/CUDA packer calls fail closed before physical work for a non-TypedRelationBlock value.

cuda_local: runtime CUDA capability and OOM handling
preserved_boundaries.semantic_authority: TypedRelationBlock/Fourfold semantics remain authoritative; this experiment contract is only shared diagnostic admission for the two physical probe arms.

finding.summary: The residual single-block semantic admission duplication is removed with one existing-module helper rather than a new layer. Pair-level Fourfold composition rules remain centralized, while CPU/CUDA retain only their physical representation and device constraints.
finding.negative_result: This packet establishes no GPU speedup, Tensor-Core use, production Tensor adoption, Tensor-vs-Forest superiority, benchmark superiority, or Gate progress.
